cards.title: How to read the race
cards.body:
The vertical axis is Arena Elo: a rough measure of how good a model's answers feel to people. The horizontal axis is API input cost per million tokens, on a log scale. Upper-left is the destination: smarter and cheaper.

I use this deliberately rough academic ladder to make the vertical movement tangible:

  • 1100 — HS freshman
  • 1200 — HS graduate
  • 1300 — College junior
  • 1350 — College graduate
  • 1400 — Master's student
  • 1450 — PhD candidate
  • 1480 — Tenured professor

The visible race starts in March 2023, when comparable Arena-era Elo begins. Older GPT-3 API models remain in elo.csv as historical metadata, but without comparable Elo they do not appear on this chart. Green points are the best price-quality frontier. The interesting points are not just the highest models, but the kinks: models that jut unusually far up-left relative to their frontier neighbors.

cards.title: March 2023 — The race begins
cards.body:
The left edge already has a useful spread. GPT-3.5 Turbo sits around Elo 1141 — HS freshman territory — at $2/M. GPT-4 lands at 1288 for $30/M: it clears the HS-graduate line and almost reaches college junior in one jump.

The first lesson is stark: intelligence arrived faster than affordability. From here, the story is how successive models climb the academic ladder while the frontier keeps moving left.

cards.title: November 2023 — College junior, one-third the price
cards.body:
GPT-4 Turbo reaches Elo 1313, the first model here to clear the college-junior line. At $10/M, it also costs one-third as much on input as the original GPT-4.

That combination matters more than either number alone. From here on, the frontier usually advances diagonally: up in intelligence while moving left in price.

cards.title: 2024 — Cheap models start reshaping the frontier
cards.body:
Claude 3 Haiku reaches Elo 1262 at $0.25/M and makes a conspicuous bend in the frontier. Then Gemma 2 9B reaches 1267 for $0.03/M. In log-price/Elo space, it is the largest local kink in this series: roughly 138 Elo above the straight line between its neighboring frontier points.

GPT-4o mini then reaches 1318 for $0.15/M. College-junior-level intelligence, which cost $10/M less than a year earlier, is suddenly available for cents. The leftward race is now as important as the upward one.

cards.title: Late 2024 — Reasoning breaks two ceilings
cards.body:
o1-preview reaches Elo 1389, the first model here past the college-graduate line (1350). December's o1 reaches 1402, crossing the master's-student line (1400).

This is mostly a vertical leap — $15/M is not cheap — but it changes the direction of model design. Spending inference-time compute to reason before answering opens a new capability path.

links.text: OpenAI: Learning to reason with LLMs

cards.title: January 2025 — Reasoning gets a price shock
cards.body:
DeepSeek R1 reaches Elo 1398 for $0.70/M: almost the same intelligence as o1 at $15/M, about 21× cheaper on input. Geometrically it is a real kink too — about 31 Elo above the local frontier chord.

The reaction was unusually large because the chart's economics suddenly mattered to everyone, not just API buyers. DeepSeek triggered a global debate about whether frontier capability really required frontier spending, alongside a historic Nvidia sell-off.

cards.title: Mid-2025 — The PhD line falls
cards.body:
Gemini 2.5 Flash reaches 1420 for $0.15/M, another sharp value kink. Then Gemini 2.5 Pro reaches 1476 for $1.25/M, the first model in this data above the PhD-candidate line (1450).

The important shape is the shelf: near the top model sits a much cheaper model only one academic rung below. Routing starts to make more sense than choosing a single default model.

cards.title: Late 2025 — The tenured-professor line falls
cards.body:
Gemini 3 Pro reaches Elo 1485 at $2/M, the first point here above the tenured-professor line (1480). One month later Gemini 3 Flash sits at 1473 for $0.50/M.

The gap between peak intelligence and cheap intelligence is no longer measured in academic stages. It is measured in a handful of Elo points.

cards.title: 2026 — The professor line races left
cards.body:
By October 2026 the upper frontier is a staircase: Gemma 4 31B at 1453/$0.09; GLM 5.3 Flash at 1473/$0.15; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at 1474/$0.20 using DeepInfra's non-promotional Standard rate; Mimo V2.6 Pro at 1480/$0.43; Gemini 3.8 Flash at 1495/$0.75; Claude Opus 5.5 at 1504/$4.

Compared with March 2023 GPT-4, Mimo is 192 Elo higher and about 70× cheaper on input. Even the 1480 threshold moves from $2 with Gemini 3 Pro in November 2025 to $0.43 ten months later — about 4.7× cheaper.

That is the central story of the chart: intelligence first climbed the academic ladder; then, increasingly, the same intelligence swept left across the price axis.
